title: Wallis's letter no. 52 (Buckingham, 1651), one of the four undeciphered 'challenge' letters nos. 50-53 of his 1653 cipher collection (Bodleian MS. e Mus. 203)

documents.shelfmark: Bodleian MS. e Mus. 203, letter 52 (EMLO 86e81b88); witness used: Davys, An Essay on the Art of Decyphering (London 1737) pp. 24-25
documents.date: undated (1651, before Charles II's march into England)
documents.route: Scotland -> Lancashire (Buckingham to an English royalist)

plaintext.source: John Davys, An Essay on the Art of Decyphering (1737) pp. 24-29: interlinear decipherment, key table and notes on the open groups (archive.org bim_eighteenth-century_an-essay-on-the-art-of-d_davys-john_1737, leaves n31-n36).

transcription.source: Davys 1737 printed pages (archive.org scans), not the manuscript
transcription.notes: Printed type; every group legible. The manuscript itself was not seen.

system.summary: Item A: numbers 1-65 single letters with 2-3 homophones, 66-455 an alphabetical table of syllables and words (82 able ... 455 you), 460-506 number codes; items B-D unseen.
system.notes: System fields describe item A (no. 52) only. The four letters are probably four different ciphers; split them once B-D are seen.

prior_solution.where: Davys, An Essay on the Art of Decyphering (London 1737) pp. 24-29, for item A only

conditions.human_role: Pasted the catalogue task; no other input.

solution.what: Digital Bodleian and EMLO: no images of MS. e Mus. 203 or Eng. misc. e. 475. Auction photographs (8) fetched: none shows letters 50-53.
Dominic Winter lot 375 description: Davys 1737 printed the Buckingham letter (no. 52). Davys 1737 found on archive.org: letter 52 printed with interlinear decipherment, key and notes (pp. 24-29).
Thurloe SP i (April 1653) searched for a Brasset to Bordeaux clear copy as a crib for no. 50: none.
Letter 52 transcribed from Davys's page images with his reading aligned group for group (letter52_davys.txt, letter52_ct.txt).

check52.py: key built from the alignment; clashes only case, i/I and u/v, plus two forced values (118 county/counte-, 144 dy/di); letters 1-65 homophonic, 66-455 alphabetical syllable/word table. 456/480 groups read (95.0%).

Open names placed by the alphabetical table: 71 (a-block, Argyle fits), 254 (between lord and London, an L name), 277 (between ly and man: Leslie per Davys, or Massey). Not decided; not written into the reading.

Audit sections I and J. letter52_plain.txt read as sentences and reviewed (grade A; check52.py re-run: 480 groups, 456 with a value). Documents B, C, D (letters 50, 51, 53) removed from documents[]: no ciphertext of them was ever in hand (Bodleian manuscripts not digitised), so no transcription or decryption can be listed; they stay the open catalogue entry 470 and a gap here.

outcome.method_basis: Letter no. 52 was deciphered in print by John Davys (1737); here it was transcribed from the printed page images and checked for consistency. Letters nos. 50, 51 and 53 were never seen and are not documents of this profile: they are the open catalogue entry no. 470.

credits.note: deciphered letter 52 and printed it with the key, An Essay on the Art of Decyphering (1737) pp. 24-29

gaps.item: letters 50, 51, 53 of the same collection (not documents of this profile since 14 Nov 2026; catalogue entry 470)
gaps.detail: Bodleian MS. e Mus. 203 pp. 218-226 / Eng. misc. e. 475 pp. 234-247 not digitised; no. 53 may be only in the private 2020 copy; no ciphertext of them was ever in hand
24 of 480 groups; Davys's guesses recorded in NOTES, not adopted

outcome.notes: Status in progress. Letter 52 has been deciphered in print since 1737. Letters 50, 51 and 53 were listed here as documents B-D until 14 Nov 2026 with no text; they were removed from documents[] because nothing of them was ever seen, and they remain the open catalogue entry 470 ('four unsolved' is three).

texts.label: no. 52, Buckingham to an English royalist (Lancashire rising), 1651; Davys 1737 pp. 24-25
texts.summary: The Lancashire gentlemen are ready to rise for the King and ask for a party of horse from Scotland to countenance their rising; the Lords in Scotland promise their best horse and Highland foot under 277 and Buckingham; Buckingham has leave to raise a troop of English horse and will go that way into England rather than lie disguised about London; the bearer Colonel Berkenhead, main negotiator of the Lancashire business, will give a full account.

reading_review.note: Read the word-spaced text of letter52_plain.txt as sentences: it runs as one coherent English letter from 'Sir, Since I sent to you last' to the signature. The holes are the address line, four number codes, three names and four dash groups (24 of 480 groups), none of which breaks a sentence. Rests on Davys's printed interlinear decipherment of 1737, aligned group for group in letter52_davys.txt; check52.py finds no clash beyond case, i/j and u/v.

outcome.fraction_read_source: check52.py on letter52_davys.txt: 456 of 480 cipher groups carry a value in Davys's interlinear decipherment (one of them, 291, by his emendation); 24 open.
